content: For a field extension K/k, do we have a typeclass expressing that K has a finite transcendence basis over k? This seems like the correct assumptions for automorphisms K ≃ₐ[k] K to have nice topological properties.
What topology do you want to put on this automorphism group? There are several choices.

I don't think such a typeclass exists, but you can make it very quickly via Algebra.trdeg k K < Cardinal.aleph0. Note that docs#krullTopology is already for general field extensions, see this old discussion.
IIRC Adam said that instead of a basis for opens being finite extensions, it should be f.g. extensions, which would definitely change things here.
yes in #36239 I decide to change it to f.g. extensions and prove it's a left uniform group
for local compactness I need the condition of finite transcendence basis
for right uniform group I also need finite transcendence basis EDIT: I tried to prove it and got stuck, it doesn't seems to be true actually EDIT2: I found a counterexample
It seems to a reasonable class to have!

I am quite bad with name, but something like Finite_trdeg seems ok. To check that the definition is correct you could prove that this is equivalent to being an algebraic extension of k(x_1, ..., x_n) (finding the idiomatic way of saying this).
it's a definition so no underscores or the linter will yell at you
